proof_summary: Quadratic-character sum identities show that for \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), the product of the matrices with constants \(C=m!\) and \(-C\) (the latter transposed) is skew-symmetric of odd order, so its determinant vanishes; Wilson’s half-factorial identity and a polynomial/Vandermonde moment argument make the \(-C\) factor nonsingular, forcing the first determinant to vanish. For \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), Euler’s criterion reduces the matrix modulo \(p\) to an \(m\)-th-power matrix, whose nonsingularity follows from the same moment argument and Wilson identity.
